rationale: newjordan's promoted harness (PR #233, main's submission/ at d0929e6) is in this package twice. labs/plain and labs/overseer are its plain/ and overseer/ byte for byte, with no change of ours, and play the four lab tasks. plain/, overseer/ and tests/ at the root are the same code with changes of ours that the note describes (a released lockdown orders workshops on the surface so that DF rebuilds its path index, and the wood-tool orders pause meanwhile; the loop tries a failing read again instead of exiting), and play the fresh embark (OP1). The shared dfbench_client/ is main's. Everything else it does in those games is its own work and that of the sources its declaration lists (our PR #124's tree and its lineage among them).
evidence: Source: submission/plain/ and submission/overseer/ at the published commit d0929e6a0ff8eb7144206ceed2c6588038c84a3f. Target: labs/plain/ and labs/overseer/ in this package, the same ten files unchanged (Overseer.progression_push is cited as one example, at the same lines); and plain/ and overseer/ at the root, where the cited functions (Overseer.endgame_supply and OpenPlayRules.thaw_window) are two examples that are unchanged from main's, at the lines given. Of these two copies of main's tree only the one at the root carries changes of ours, marked `h2` in the code: plain/harness.py (read, attempt, look, advance_failed, seen), overseer/openplay.py (reconnect, reindex_site and their constants), overseer/harness.py (progression_push, step), tests/test_h2_loop.py, tests/test_h2_reconnect.py and tests/test_h2_push.py. One more change of ours is in the root tree, marked `h5`: overseer/openplay.py (reconnect: past the game's allowance of release-guard workshops a release may order one more when none is waiting) and its test in tests/test_h2_reconnect.py. A second `h5` change in the root tree is in overseer/openplay.py (cull: a hunger check that marks nothing starts no cooldown), with its test in tests/test_winner_fixes.py. A third `h5` change in the root tree is in overseer/harness.py (defend: a nearest-hostile distance of 0 is a hostile on the wagon's tile, and a refused warning may be tried again a day later), with its test in tests/test_h2_reconnect.py. Overseer.meeting_area, which our packages from PR #240 to PR #249 had changed so that no underground meeting area was made on OP1, is main's rule again in this package with one condition of ours added: on OP1 the zone waits until a wildlife lockdown has begun in the game (its docstring says so, marked `h5`; one line of overseer/openplay.py counts the lockdowns; tests/test_winner_fixes.py asserts both steps).

rationale: Our own PR #229 (arm d81) is this package's controller for the handed-over fort (MY1): its plain/ and overseer/ are at ours/plain and ours/overseer (its tests are not shipped in this package; they are in our PR #250's tree), with three changes of ours that the note describes (a released lockdown orders workshops on the surface, and past the game's allowance of them one more when none is waiting, marked `h5` in ours/overseer/openplay.py; the loop tries a failing read again; an office below ground for the expedition leader, marked `h4` in ours/overseer/harness.py). dispatch/ runs it for an open task shorter than a year. Its own declaration lists what it is built on. The entries below declare directly the ten sources of that declaration that main's does not list, and seven submissions of the lineage the two trees share, which comments in the package's files name (all seven are in main's declaration, four of them in PR #229's). Declared although RULES section 8 makes one's own earlier submissions optional.

rationale: yukonautominer's published harness (PR #168) starts the hunger cull's cooldown only when the pass marked an animal: a check that found nothing it may slaughter (every animal left kept for the feast) used to start it too, so a food-zero emergency days later waited out the 5 or 8 days. This package makes the same one-line change in its own cull() on the open tasks (the lab tasks never reach it); the comment there credits them. In 366 of our local games the old rule held back such a cull in 18, inside the scored last 28 days in 7. In this package that code is in ours/, the controller for the handed-over fort (MY1), as in our e884d63b.

rationale: yukonautominer's published harness (PR #178) builds a strange mood's workshop again when the listed one has stood with its construction suspended: its mood() reads the controller's own shops(), which leaves such a workshop out, where the leader's code read the raw workshop list and waited on it for good. In this package that code is in ours/, the controller for the handed-over fort (MY1), as in our e884d63b.
